Baltasar-Kormakur: Baltasar Kormákur A true PHOTO EXPRESS job. At the last minute, I flew to North Iceland and drove from there to Hofsós, where I shot director Baltasar Kormákur in record time. As he and his wife (the beautiful Lilja Pálma, who I shot for NYT (LINK) made me coffee, I processed and sent the photos off to Grapevine HQ. I flew back to Reykjavík that night, and was greeted with a still warm, fresh off the presses copy of Grapevine bearing my image on the cover. What a rollercoaster that was!
Blue-Lagoon: Blue Lagoon I’ve always been fascinated by visual storytelling. For this Blue Lagoon campaign, I got to relay the stories of three magnificent women through my images.
East-of-the-Mountain: Austur fyrir Fjall The show Austur fyrir fjall (“East of the Mountain”) consisted of photos that I shot during my backpacking trip through Asia, from December of 2009 until May of 2010. I traveled through India, Nepal, Tibet, Vietnam and Cambodia, having eye-opening experiences at every turn and photographing the people I encountered. I like to refer to these images as “environmental portraits,” as they depict the subjects going about their day-to-day lives in their natural environment, whether it be on the coast of Goa, India, up in the Himalayas of Nepal or the Cambodian countryside. Austur fyrir Fjall opened at Skólavörðustígur, Reykjavík, on August 9, 2012. A look at the Skólavörðustígur show. Gummi Kr. and Jónína De La Rosa served as my left AND right hands while installing the show.
Gunnar-Nelson: Gunnar Nelson Rising UFC star Gunnar Nelson is without any doubt the coolest Icelander I have ever captured through my lens. And when I say cool, I don’t mean in a big, tough-guy kind of sense—more in the Zen one; Gunnar is cool, calm, and collected. He is also an absolutely admirable athlete, whose career I look forward to follow in the coming years and whom I hope to shoot again sooner than later.
GusGus: Gus Gus The boys of Gus Gus dropped by my studio for a bit of a promo session.
Jon-Gnarr: Jón Gnarr The mayor of Reykjavík, Jón Gnarr, shot infront of the City Hall. His last photoshoot before he left office. Been there done that. Inspired by Pete Sellers in Being There.
Knit-to-the-Music: Knit to the Music Ragga Eiríks and Stephen West are both accomplished knit-designers. I teamed up with them for Knit to the Music, a project where we got some of our favorite Icelandic musicians to sport Ragga and Stephen’s designs in the atmospheric settings of 101 Reykjavík’s KEX Hostel. The results were published in book form, and we also showed the photos at KEX (the opening party was wonderful!).
Metalhead: Málmhaus I had the pleasure of visiting the set while the award-winning feature film Málmhaus (“Metalhead”) was being shot in Iceland. The accompanying promo-shots for the film were the outcome of my visit, along with the sheer joy of getting to observe a large group of talented, focused people in the process of creating a work of art.
Milos-Forman: Milos Forman Prior to shooting Milos Forman, I had no idea who he was or what he did. This was probably for the best, as the knowledge that I was contending with a legendary, Oscar-winning filmmaker would probably have made me nervous. Forman arrived on location donning a pair of Crocs, and I tried very hard to get him to remove the ghastly plastic shoes. He resisted with all his might, until I gave him a cigar that I had for some reason brought along. The lure of quality tobacco enticed him to remove one of the shoes, the other firmly planted on his foot. I have learned that some people simply get away with this kind of thing, and Milos Forman is definitely one of them. Forsíða Grapevine. Milos, puffing on my cigar. It made him slightly more malleable.
Sarah-Reinertsen: Sarah Reinertsen I was fortunate enough to meet and photograph the great triathlete Sarah Reinertsen, a truly inspiring human being. The work was commissioned by Nike and prosthetics maker Össur, for their collaborative Flex-Run™ campaign.
